children: Spot premiums for Middle East crude benchmarks Oman, Dubai and Murban held steady at their three-month highs on Thursday, supported by continued supply disruptions amid rising tensions.
Oil futures prices hovered near six-week highs on Thursday after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and renewed Israeli threats against Tehran.
Six commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 11 a day earlier and well below the 10-day average of around 13, preliminary shipping data showed on Thursday.

Japan's refiner Idemitsu Kosan bought two million barrels of U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude from SK Energy at a premium of about $20 per barrel to the November Dubai benchmark, trade sources said.
Cash Dubai's premium to swaps rose 14 cents to $17.90 a barrel.
Iran has added more ships it deems as non-compliant and subject to fines, confiscation or detention if they try to sail through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a government website.
Several international energy firms, including Eni
committed on Wednesday to project expansions to boost oil output in Venezuela, in a signing ceremony in Caracas overseen by interim President Delcy Rodriguez and U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright.

Russia will slightly reduce its oil output this year, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Thursday, but the situation is temporary and oil production will begin to increase once domestic refineries finish scheduled maintenance.

As China learns to live on less fuel since the Iran war, its carbon emissions are falling, a new analysis showed on Thursday, with researchers saying a structural shift towards electrification and cleaner transport was creating the conditions for emissions' sustained decline.
